children: By George Glover and Anita Hamilton
Apple managed to escape the artificial-intelligence panic that sparked last week's stock market rout — but there may be tougher times ahead for the tech giant.

The iPhone 18 launch probably won't go as well as Apple wants because customers will find it tough to stomach higher prices when their existing device already does the job, KeyBanc analyst Brandon Nispel wrote in a note recapping a survey of iPhone users.

"Below the surface, the broader base of consumers are less likely to upgrade as prices rise, carriers restrict promotions, and their existing hardware is adequate," he said. "This ultimately leads to a moderation in unit volumes."
Nispel rates Apple at Underweight and has a $250 price target, which implies a 27% drop from the stock's close on Friday.
Apple dodged the broader market gloom last week, lifting its total market capitalization to more than $5 trillion for the first time ever.

And it's got more tricks up its sleeve. On Monday, Bloomberg reported that that company will unveil its first touch-screen MacBook at its Oct. 28 "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles. That comes on the heels its foldable Duo phone last month and HomeView smart home hub earlier this month. Apple didn't immediately reply to Barron's request for comment on coming announcements.

Apple stock was basically flat, but holding its market cap above the $5 trillion mark. The worry for investors is that the company's earnings won't rise fast enough to justify that lofty valuation. Shares fetch 36-times expected earnings for fiscal 2027, a sizable premium to their historical average.
But one point in Apple's favor is that it hasn't plowed much money into AI, compared with rivals like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon who plan to pour hundreds of billions of dollars into the tech.

Plenty of investors don't think this year's 26% rally will last but Apple is "the poster child for how the market is rewarding a capex-lite approach that is AI-model agnostic," said Melius analyst Ben Reitzes, who rates the stock at Buy with a $370 price target.
